text:
Maya (Sales): Heads-up 1024 FinCo RFP landed. Key asks: per-tenant capacity guarantees, routing by latency SLAs, and a 99.9% inference availability commitment. They want a firm pilot timeline for procurement.

Ava (PM): Can we do a quick assessment here? Sales needs a yes/no for committing to a pilot timeline by EOD tomorrow.

Raj (Eng): Short answer: we can scope a pilot but full product work is non-trivial. Rough ballpark: 2w design + 40w infra/runtime + 1w testing = 7-9 weeks for a hardened ship. If we accept a more limited pilot (soft caps, routing shim) we can aim for 4w.

Liam (SE): Proposed pilot scope (minimal viable):
````
Pilot acceptance (MVP-shim):
- Soft per-tenant GPU caps (enforced at scheduler level) + alerting
- Simple latency-tier routing (low / standard) with deterministic fallback
- Tenant-scoped audit events for routing/model decisions
- Customer-facing risk doc & manual rollback procedure
````
Keep advanced batching, q8 quant profiles, and autoscale integration out of scope.

Priya (CS): FinCo flagged compliance: they need CNTRL mapping for isolation controls. If we can't guarantee physical isolation we should provide a SOC2 mapping and signed risk acknowledgment. CS must be involved in pilot runbook.

Noah (Design): UX ask is minimal: a console control to set tenant caps and pick latency tier. I'll deliver a low-fidelity mock and a simple form for pilot. No need for polished UX now.

Jordan (CTO): Two product questions: is this a one-off enterprise request or a broader signal we should bake into roadmap? And if we prioritize, what feature(s) do we deprioritize? We have limited cycles.

Ava (PM): It's both: big logo opportunity AND it highlights platform-level gaps (capacity controls, routing). Proposal: greenlight a scoped pilot (Liam's MVP-shim) and temporarily postpone the 'quality-regression-detector' eval sprint by one cadence. That frees 2 engineers for ~5 weeks.

Raj (Eng): If we shift the eval sprint, Eng can reassign two ICs + Eng-SRE support. We still need a canary plan: start on non-prod, then a single-tenant prod canary, then gradual ramp. Also need a fallback path to single-model routing.

Maya (Sales): If we can give FinCo a firm pilot start (exact date) and a rollback plan, I can push them for an LOI. They said pricing is secondary to predictable latency and isolation.

Priya (CS): Add to acceptance: runbook with failover steps, compliance artifact checklist, and a tenant-load test harness. CS will own the runbook and coordinate legal for the risk acknowledgment.

Liam (SE): I'll draft a load harness and simple route policy YAML for the pilot. Early snippet: 
```
route_policy:
  - id: low
    max_p95_ms: 60
    fallback: standard
  - id: standard
    max_p95_ms: 300
```
Also will provide a script to simulate tenant burst patterns.

Noah (Design): Mock uploaded: https://redwood.mock/finco/tenant-caps-v1 (low-fi). Will attach to the customer doc once PR is merged.

Jordan (CTO): If we push the eval sprint, we need commitment from Product + Eng to ship the pilot scope and a customer-facing risk doc. Otherwise we tell FinCo earliest start is next quarter.

Ava (PM): Quick vote: greenlight scoped pilot + pause eval sprint?

Raj (Eng): +1 if Eng-SRE supports autoscale testing and we keep the scope tight. Need sign-off from SRE by EOD.

Maya (Sales): +1. I'll give FinCo an 8-week pilot window with the scoped feature set and an explicit risk acknowledgment.

Priya (CS): +1. I'll have the runbook & compliance checklist draft by Friday COB.

Liam (SE): +1. Test harness will be ready for SRE to run canary tests.

Ava (PM): Next actions:
- Raj to confirm resource reassignments and SRE support by EOD
- Noah to attach mock and brief screenshots
- Priya + Liam to pair on runbook + load tests
- Maya to request LOI with an 8-week pilot timeline (conditional on getting the risk doc)

deploy-bot: Pipeline created for branch: feat/tenant-cap-shim. No automatic prod deploy until canary gates pass.

Ava (PM): We'll reconvene tomorrow 9:30am PT to finalize the customer-facing pilot doc and timeline. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
